name: Glassdoor
description: Glassdoor is an employment community for researching jobs, companies, salaries, interviews, workplace reviews, and employer brands. Job seekers and employers use its profiles, community content, hiring services, and Indeed-linked application experiences.
agentUseSummary: Glassdoor cannot currently be connected through Relay. Its remaining public API documentation describes account-tied partner credentials and mandatory end-user attribution, but the documented API endpoint now returns HTTP 410 and the current site terms prohibit automated agents, scraping, stripping, or mining without express approval. Glassdoor account, community, application, employer, and anonymous-review data have no current distributable OAuth or API contract for Relay.

blocked.label: Connect a Glassdoor account
blocked.description: Glassdoor does not publish a current supported third-party customer-account API, OAuth application contract, token lifecycle, scopes, or revocation interface for Relay.

blocked.label: Read Glassdoor companies, jobs, or salaries
blocked.description: The documented partner-key endpoint for company search now returns HTTP 410; jobs, salaries, interviews, and non-public API actions are unavailable without a current approved contract.

blocked.label: Read Glassdoor account or hiring data
blocked.description: Profiles, resumes, applications, messages, saved activity, employer dashboards, candidate data, advertising data, and Indeed-connected information remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Use Glassdoor reviews or community content
blocked.description: Reading, summarizing, submitting, moderating, correlating, or attempting to identify anonymous reviews, salaries, interviews, posts, comments, groups, or community members is blocked.

blocked.label: Automate Glassdoor services
blocked.description: Automated agents, scraping, stripping, mining, private interfaces, browser automation, cookie or credential capture, bulk extraction, and raw requests outside a current approved API are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Glassdoor action is enabled until Glassdoor publishes or grants Relay a current HTTPS API contract with exact distribution, attribution, end-user, privacy, anonymity, retention, and revocation terms.

runtimeSupport.description: The documented Glassdoor public API endpoint is retired, and current terms require express approval for automated agents.
The documented Glassdoor public API endpoint is retired, and current terms require express approval for automated agents.

providerSetup.blocker: Glassdoor still serves legacy public API registration and documentation pages for account-tied partner IDs and keys, company search, end-user IP and user-agent forwarding, and mandatory attribution. However, the documented `api.glassdoor.com/api/api.htm` endpoint returns HTTP 410 over HTTPS, the legacy examples use HTTP, non-public actions require an API partnership, and the current July 2026 terms restrict the services to personal non-commercial use absent a separate agreement and prohibit introducing automated agents or scraping, stripping, or mining without express approval. No current delegated account API or OAuth contract is documented.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Glassdoor credentials or show Connect. Reconsider only if Glassdoor provides Relay a current HTTPS endpoint and exact approved application contract. The provider-console owner must obtain written confirmation of available actions, authentication, end-user IP and user-agent handling, attribution and display, anonymous-content treatment, caching and retention, redistribution, Indeed data separation, rate limits, key rotation, revocation, deletion, and agent use. Only then should Relay implement bounded typed reads and any separately approved mutations.

evidence.supports: Glassdoor's remaining API overview documents legacy REST GET requests with partner ID and key, end-user IP and user-agent parameters, mandatory attribution, and separate non-public partner APIs.
Glassdoor's public company action documentation describes employer search and result metadata under legacy API version 1 with account-assigned partner credentials.
Glassdoor's registration page says an API key is tied to a Glassdoor account and requires login or account creation to obtain one.
The HTTPS form of Glassdoor's documented API endpoint returned HTTP 410 during a credential-free HEAD request, so Relay cannot treat the legacy documentation as a live supported transport.
Glassdoor's current July 2026 terms require a separate agreement for commercial use and prohibit automated agents, scraping, stripping, or mining without express approval.
Glassdoor emphasizes protection of reviewer anonymity and restrictions on employer attempts to identify or coerce reviewers.
